tests_run.name: mcp_analysis_disasm_at_path_arm_on_x64_pe
tests_run.result: ok (Capstone arm backend reachable via generic dispatcher)
tests_run.note: Disassembled bytes are nonsensical as ARM because the binary is an x86_64 PE; this only confirms backend wiring, not semantic correctness. No A32/T32 binary present in baseline corpus.

overlap_analysis: The validator for rustre-arch-arm is a static parser of the crate's documentation report (functions/signatures), not a behavioral comparator. The crate exposes A32/T32/NEON/VFP decoders and CPU semantics, reachable from MCP only through the generic `analysis_disasm_at_path` dispatcher (arch=arm) - there is no dedicated `analysis_disasm_at_path_arm` tool (unlike arm64/cil/jvm/mips/riscv/wasm). The baseline corpus contains only cargo-zyphora.exe (x86_64 PE), so MCP cannot exercise the ARM backend on a real ARM target. Functional disasm comparison between MCP and validator is therefore not feasible with the current corpus; the validator's static contract (27 exported functions across 5 modules) is satisfied.
